scenes.headline: How a per-option scorer runs in a browser tab
scenes.sub: A Jev-shaped model on WebGPU and WASM, and what its isolation costs.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ivy! Can a model shaped like Jev run inside your browser tab? It can. Here's how.

scenes.text: A per-option scorer is easy to ship to a browser. The costly part is its guarantee: every option scored alone, with its own copy of the context.
scenes.say: The model is the easy part: an encoder, and a head with one output. The hard part is its guarantee.

steps.say: The tab pairs the context with each option. So every row carries its own full copy of the context.
Each row runs through a small cross-encoder, on WebAssembly, or WebGPU if your browser has one.
Out comes a short row of logits. Keep the entailment column, and each option has one score.

steps.note: an option's probability depends on what else is listed
steps.say: Then a softmax across them all. Nothing in the code knows how many options there are: N is a loop bound.

scenes.title: Two ways to score N options

left.title: Isolated rows, like Jev
items: Context copied into every option's row
The encoder runs once per option
left.say: Jev keeps each option in its own row, so no option sees its neighbours. The price: the context is encoded again for every option.

right.title: One shared sequence
items: Every option is a marked span
Encode once, read N logits out
right.say: The other shape packs every option into one sequence and encodes once. Both open System One models chose it. That's why they're fast.

scenes.label: the tokens option isolation costs at sixteen options: 784 against 126
scenes.say: With one tokenizer on identical content, that isolation costs six point two times the tokens at sixteen options.

scenes.label: the logits shape of the only open System One ONNX export
scenes.note: 25 candidates, fixed when the graph was exported
scenes.say: And the export changes N itself. The only open System One model with a browser playground outputs twenty-five logits, every time. The option count becomes a tensor shape.

scenes.text: The hard part of running Jev in a browser is not the model. It is the guarantee.

recap: Each option gets its own row and one score
Isolation costs 6.2× the tokens at sixteen options
The ONNX export fixes the output at 25
scenes.say: To recap: one row per option, a price in tokens for that isolation, and an export that turns N into a shape.
